solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thrills jerks

definitions.meaning: thrills or excitement, as in doing something for the buzz of it
sharp sudden movements, like those of a leg or a gun's recoil

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are plural nouns: excitements sought for fun, and sudden jolting movements.

clue.text: Rook pinned in by two other pieces — that's fishy

parts.note: a king is one chess piece

indicators.note: pinned in means trapped between, so the letter sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a pawn is another chess piece
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess position where a rook is pinned by two pieces, something dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinned' is a chess term, but here R goes inside PAWN. A prawn is a crustacean, not strictly a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This large shellfish is seafood, loosely something from the fish counter.

clue.text: Bread and tea to be served on terrace shortly

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another sits above it

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a patio is a paved terrace

explanation.surface: Bread and tea are brought out onto the patio soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims PATIO to PATI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened Indian flatbread.

clue.text: Almost suffer getting pulled before start of sandwich course

indicators.note: getting simply joins the next piece on
before says the earlier piece leads
almost means not quite, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to stand something is to suffer or put up with it
drew is the past of draw, to pull

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Nearly enduring a drag ahead of a sandwich course at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a meal; St Andrews is a famous golf course in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Course at St Andrews is the historic home of golf.

clue.text: Creeps having relationship that may be cast off

indicators.note: having signals that one piece is followed by the other in a simple string

parts.note: creeps as a noun are unpleasant people, slangily called snakes
kin are relations, family ties

explanation.surface: Unpleasant types have a bond with someone who might be dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creeps' reads as a verb, but it is a plural noun for nasty people.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent sloughs its outer covering periodically, so this is literally the thing that is shed.

clue.text: Knock off heroin in bar

indicators.note: in places the one piece inside the other

parts.note: bar can mean except, as can save
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A drug dealer gets knocked off in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: To shave a price is to knock a little off it.

clue.text: Posted in a mobile home for Anzacs

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Mail delivered to a caravan for Australian and New Zealand soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Anzacs are Australian and New Zealand troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia and New Zealand, the far side of the world from Britain, are called the Antipodes.

clue.text: Mount some asymmetric trophies

indicators.note: mount means climb, and in a down clue going up reads the letters backwards
some says only part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Display some lopsided awards on a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: SYMME, read upwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These statuettes are American television awards.

clue.text: County doctor from long ago

definitions.meaning: a county in the Republic of Ireland
Dr ..., hero of a 1960s US TV medical drama

explanation.definitionFit: An Irish county shares its name with a TV doctor from the 1960s.

clue.text: Ignorance is a terrible thing

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters are badly mangled

explanation.surface: A saying that not knowing things is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is a figure for ignorance, as in being in the dark.

clue.text: Get to retreat before half of foreign peninsula falls

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the second
retreating means going backwards, so the word for get is read in reverse

parts.note: to get something is to gain it

indicators.note: half of says only the first three of six letters are kept

parts.note: Arabia is a peninsula abroad, in south-west Asia

explanation.surface: An instruction to withdraw before part of an overseas headland collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' turns GAIN into NIAG; 'half of' cuts ARABIA down to ARA.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border bear this name.

clue.text: Delay treatment of unnamed ligament

indicators.note: giving something a treatment works it over, so the letters are rearranged
N is the abbreviation for name, so unnamed means that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A medical holdup while an anonymous torn tendon gets seen to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' removes N (name) from LIGAMENT, leaving LIGAMET; 'treatment of' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap in time between cause and effect is a hold-up or delay.

clue.text: Tartan army's leader invading pitch, teasing out cover

indicators.note: teasing is taken loosely as itching or tickling, so an ITCH is pulled out of the word pitch
invading means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lid is a cover, as on a pan

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Scotland's football fans storm the field, led by their chief, after a whipped-off blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tartan Army is the name for Scotland's football supporters, but here 'Tartan' alone is the definition. 'teasing out' removes ITCH from 'pitch', leaving P; A goes into P + LID.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaid is a woven chequered cloth, the pattern Scots call tartan.

clue.text: By the way, The Guardian ultimately wants to change a worker

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: to pass is to change, as when a title passes to an heir
an ant is the classic crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A newspaper's aside: the paper eventually wishes to swap one of its employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants to' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in English to mean incidentally, in passing.

clue.text: Wound core of ordinary cable that contains shock?

indicators.note: wound as in coiled or twisted, so the letters are turned about
the core is the inside of the word, so its outer pairs O-R and R-Y are stripped away

explanation.surface: Wrapped-up innards of a standard electric lead that holds a jolt of electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core of' keeps DINA from ORDINARY; 'Wound' mixes DINA with CABLE. A 'shock' here is a mass of hair, not an electric jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: This hair band holds back a thick head of hair, which is called a shock.

clue.text: Grasp head following struggle in hospital department

indicators.note: following says this piece comes after
in places the one piece within the other

parts.note: A and E is the accident and emergency department
war is struggle
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Grasp the boss after a fight in the casualty ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is understanding, a grasp of a situation.

clue.text: Young man's back, but not before start of work

indicators.note: not before means coming after, so this piece follows the other
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to back someone is to support or help them

explanation.surface: A lad is supportive, though not ahead of the working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link; 'not before' puts HELP after W.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky or impudent youth is dismissively called a pup, cub or the like.

clue.text: Depress radio version of the King's swansong?

indicators.note: on the radio a thing is heard, not seen, so it sounds like the words

parts.note: Way Down was Elvis Presley's last single in his lifetime

explanation.surface: A sad broadcast of a monarch's final performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley.
explanation.definitionFit: To press heavily on something is to depress it physically or in spirits.

clue.text: Alien in hole is buried under pressure over little green things?

indicators.note: in a down clue, buried under means coming below the previous piece
in puts the one piece inside the other

parts.note: a pit is a hole
ET is the film alien
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A green alien is buried in a pit under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little green things' suggests aliens; the setter later said 'things' should read 'thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petits pois are tiny garden peas, small green vegetables.

clue.text: Steals nothing, according to report

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A news item says someone takes things and yet takes nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: To nick is British slang for to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicks is British slang meaning pinches or pilfers.

clue.text: Cut short hanging with altered hem?

indicators.note: the hem is the edge, so the end letter is changed

parts.note: a curtain is a hanging

explanation.surface: Shorten a drape whose hem has been taken up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered hem' swaps the final N of CURTAIN for L.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short or reduce.

clue.text: Attacker got out of very powerless police trap

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction for very, as in allegro assai

indicators.note: P stands for power, so powerless takes that letter out

parts.note: a plant is something hidden by police to incriminate or entrap

explanation.surface: An assailant slipped free of a feeble police snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got out of' links; 'powerless' drops P from PLANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who assails, or physically attacks, another person.

clue.text: Not one person settled, take it for granted

definitions.meaning: if no one has paid, everybody owes

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, 'all owed' says nobody has settled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Granted or conceded, as in being allowed something.

clue.text: Sort of Rent-a-Mess?

indicators.note: to sort something can mean to rearrange it, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek agency hiring out chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a muddle or a supposed discovery that proves illusory, which fits a hired-in mess.

clue.text: Cram face completely

parts.note: mug is slang for face
up means completely, as in eat up

explanation.surface: A face entirely stuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug up is British slang for cramming for an exam.

clue.text: Women roughly right to interrupt sketch

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a skit is a comic sketch

explanation.surface: Females rudely break into a comedy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' marks crude slang for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirt is crude slang for women, as in bit of skirt.

clue.text: Wife wearing short stunning number reveals strap

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the letter goes inside
short means cut, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a taser stuns, so it numbs: a number

explanation.surface: A wife dressed in a short glamorous outfit shows a strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a numbing device, here a taser; 'short' trims it to TASE. A tawse is a Scottish leather punishment strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A tawse is a leather strap used for punishment in Scottish schools.

clue.text: He scored, left mobbed by crowd

indicators.note: being mobbed means surrounded, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a host is a large crowd, as in a host of angels

explanation.surface: A footballer scored, then went off and was swamped by fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests a goal; it means writing a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst composed and scored music such as The Planets.

clue.text: Rock and rolled in Provençal cottage?

indicators.note: in places the one piece within the other

parts.note: a gite is a French holiday cottage
to roll is to run, as a ball runs along

explanation.surface: Rock and roll goes on in a holiday home in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and rolled' looks like rock'n'roll, but 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock.

clue.text: Show how novel is a collection of biographies

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Demonstrate how a book of fiction counts as a group of life stories.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a reference book of short entries on notable people's lives.

clue.text: Chivalry demands single woman to be put in post

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside the other piece

parts.note: a pole is a post
I is the Roman numeral one, single
Tess is a woman's name, as in Hardy's Tess

explanation.surface: Gallantry insists that an unmarried lady be given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demands' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Politesse is formal courtesy, a refined manner akin to chivalry.

clue.text: Result of undies one stripped off?

definitions.text: Result of undies one stripped off?

indicators.note: the result of treating the letters is something rearranged from them
stripped off means removed, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: What you get when someone takes their underwear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped off' removes I from UNDIES; 'Result of' rearranges UNDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked figures are what is left once underwear is removed.
